data_section_full_text:
2.1. Sample and Data

I begin with all 10-K (and 10-K SB) and 10-Q (and 10-Q SB) filings for the study
period from January 1, 1996 to December 31, 2001, which I identify from the
EDGAR header files. <sup>14</sup> These number 48,228 10-Ks (and 13,315 10-K SBs) and
181,599 10-Qs (and 52,214 10-Q SBs). I then select filings for those companies that
are also listed in the CRSP population. <sup>15,16</sup> This set numbers 12,372 10-K (and
4,335 10-K SB) and 58,474 10-Q (and 10,330 10-Q SB) filings. These filings
represent 3634 individual registrant companies (based on the 10-Ks). The CRSP
daily return and market capitalization data requirements then reduce these
numbers to 10,805 10-K and 52,262 10-Q filings. The CRSP data requirement also
reduces the number of individual registrants to 3382 companies. <sup>17</sup> Equivalently, the
CRSP data requirement reduces the SB samples to 2991 Form 10-K SB and 6,797
Form 10-Q SB filings, representing 910 individual companies (based on the 10-Ks).
Thus, the merged SEC/CRSP samples represent approximately 26% of all 10-Ks
and 32% of all 10-Qs. Also, the proportion of 10-K SB or 10-Q SB filings to all
filings of a given form type is approximately 22%. As such, prior research on SEC
